attributes.readMe:
# Meeting

## Summary
A meeting with `meetingType` (interview | one-on-one | standup | vendor-review), `date` (datetime), `duration` (DurationField), an optional linked `candidate`, `interviewers` (linksToMany Employee), a `roundType` (InterviewRoundField), an `interviewScore` (ScoreField), an optional `scorecard` (ScorecardField) and markdown `notes`.

## Import
```ts
import { Meeting } from './meeting';
```

## Usage — three or more ways this is used

**1. As a calendar event.** The Calendar tab maps these into `CalendarEvent`
objects; `date` is a DateTimeField and drag-to-reschedule preserves the
original time of day while replacing the date.

**2. As the interview scorecard.** `interviewScore` (ScoreField, 1–5) is rolled
up per candidate into an average shown on the pipeline board as `★ 4.3 avg · 3`.
The optional `scorecard` field carries a structured per-criterion breakdown
plus a hire/no-hire recommendation for interviews that need more than one
number.

**3. As the panel record.** `candidate` plus `interviewers` (linksToMany
Employee) record who met whom; both are denormalized into `candidateName` and
`interviewerTally` so the fitted view can show them without resolving links.

**4. As an overdue-feedback signal.** A meeting whose `date` has passed with no
`interviewScore` is derived as `Score overdue` — the one state a scheduling
card can legitimately surface, and it comes free from date + score.

**5. As a typed activity.** `meetingType` (interview | one-on-one | standup |
vendor-review) colours the event chip so the calendar reads at a glance;
`roundType` (phone-screen | technical | onsite | panel | final) further
classifies interview meetings specifically.

## Template Usage
Isolated view renders `<@fields.scorecard />` and `<@fields.roundType />` in
the main panel/details sidebar when present. Embedded view shows type, time,
duration, candidate, and score.

**Example in use:** `Meeting/interview-amara-1` carries `roundType: technical`
and a 3-criterion `scorecard` (Problem Solving, Communication, Culture Fit)
with a `hire` recommendation.

**Non-goals:** recurrence rules; external calendar sync; video-call links.
